events.name: Intersect Austin
events.note: Free public show on Saturday, noon–5 PM. Ticketed extras: early access on Saturday, 10 AM–noon, and Intersect After Dark on Friday, 6–9 PM.

events.name: Minutes + Hours Austin
events.note: The first 100 guests each day receive a free Europa Star magazine and a Minutes + Hours tote bag, and are entered to win watches and prizes — including watches from Haim, Venezianico, Farr + Swit, Mad Hudson and G-SHOCK.

events.name: Minutes + Hours: An Evening for Collectors
events.note: A preview evening at M Robinson Fine Jewelers in Bee Cave with three brands, plus a curated collection of pre-owned Rolex and other watches. Open bar, whiskey, and light fare.

releases.text:
Teaser — A brand-new Baltic line, teased October 22 with color and texture as its stated focus.

Hermétique The Rift — A limited edition of the Hermétique field watch tied to The Rift gravel race in Iceland, and the first Hermétique offered in a smaller 34mm size alongside the 37mm. Fully luminous white dial with a forged carbon track and Icelandic landscape colors; Miyota 9039.
Price: €620 excluding taxes (€744 including VAT)
Availability: Sold out in both 34mm and 37mm.

Aquascaphe GMT MK-II — The second-generation Aquascaphe GMT switches to a Miyota 9075 true traveler GMT with a jumping local hour. The redesigned 39.5mm case adds crown guards and doubles water resistance to 200m; four sapphire-bezel color options.
Price: €850 on rubber strap / €915 on steel bracelet, excluding taxes

Facet 41 — A larger 41mm version of Circula's integrated-bracelet Facet, after the 38mm original of 2024. The faceted design runs through the case, the gearwheel-embossed dial and the hands; four dial colors with a color-matched date at 6, on an integrated steel bracelet or leather strap. La Joux-Perret G100.
Price: $1,690 on leather strap / $1,990 on the integrated steel bracelet

Canford Automatic — The Canford, Elliot Brown's founding model, reworked as an automatic in a smaller 39mm dual-crown case: a lockable internal timing bezel, a Miyota 9015 automatic with date, a display back and 200m of water resistance. Six references, 303-A61 to A66, from an opaline-white dial to a black-PVD case.
Price: £795 ($906)

Essence Ceramica Dark Matter Redshift — A new variant of the 41mm full-ceramic Essence Ceramica: a sandblasted black ceramic case and bracelet around Formex's Case Suspension System, with a solid Muonionalusta meteorite dial under a black-gold coating and red "Redshift" accents. COSC-certified Sellita SW200-2, 65-hour reserve; 100 pieces a year, the inaugural series numbered 001–100.
Price: CHF 3,500 / $4,450
Availability: First shipments end of November 2026.

Bio Bay Terrazzo — A new Bio Bay model with a terrazzo-inspired dial: 39mm steel case with fixed lugs, a Miyota quartz movement, sapphire crystal and 100m water resistance.
Price: $175
Availability: Delivery estimated early December 2026.

Isotope × Direnzo — DRZ 08 Cosmonaire GMT — Isotope's edition of the DRZ 08 Cosmonaire, Direnzo's new first GMT: a gray layered dial with heat-blued hands in the model's 39mm coated-steel case with an elliptical bezel; Sellita SW330-2. One of the Cosmonaire's two limited editions, alongside a 60-piece meteorite version.
Price: CHF 1,350 at launch / CHF 1,400 retail
Availability: Launches Sat Nov 21, 2026, 15:00 CET; delivery mid-January 2027; 40 pieces.

Flyway Coral — A new colorway of the Flyway: a coral dial stamped with a pyramid pattern in a 36mm wing-shaped steel case, under a hyperbolic paraboloid sapphire crystal — a saddle-shaped geometry that keeps the dial distortion-free and legible from a wide range of angles. A choice of Landeron or La Joux-Perret G101 automatics; 100 pieces.
Price: £1,200 (Landeron) / £1,496 (La Joux-Perret G101)

Strat-o-timer 42 GMT Dr Pepper Limited Edition — revisits the Texas brands’ collaboration with a black dial, red bezel accents and gold-tone details. Limited to 230 pieces.
Price: $1,299
Status: Sold out

Strat-o-timer GMT Triton Meteorite — The Strat-o-timer's first meteorite dial. The icy blue dial is cut from the Muonionalusta meteorite and acid-etched, so no two are alike. A 40mm steel case, a navy and red ceramic GMT bezel, and the Miyota 9075 traveler GMT movement. Limited production of 200 pieces.
Price: $1,449
Availability: Sold out; expected shipping the week of November 16.

Jacques Bianchi Marseille × Deepsea.EDC — JB300 Professional (forged carbon) — A new JB300 developed with Deepsea.EDC's Brock Stevens: a forged-carbon case over a Grade 5 titanium core with fixed FXD-style lugs, a left-hand crown and a matte black no-date maxi dial. The Soprod P024 is now COSC-certified; 41.5mm, 300m, with a fully lumed bezel whose first 15 minutes glow green against blue.
Price: $1,950 (€1,995)
Availability: Preorders start Nov 3, 2026 on the brand's website; limited to 500 pieces (300 public, 200 reserved for the Unit Watch Program); estimated delivery April 2027.

Model No. 2b Chronograph — The first of Lorca's b-Series, the Model No. 2b reworks the Model No. 2 Chronograph as a more utilitarian instrument: a matte black printed dial with matte white subdials, brushed hands, and a fully brushed, engraved 12-hour bezel in place of the polished guilloché. The 37mm case and hand-wound Sellita SW510 M carry over unchanged.
Price: $2,750
Availability: Limited initial production of 20 pieces; shipping expected by the end of November 2026.

Deep, Black Destro / Blue Orthodox / Polar Destro / Ember — The Deep leaves the Sector Series to stand as its own model, marked by a limited run of 300 with a new movement: Miyota's 8315, 60-hour reserve, with striped decoration and blued screws. The 500-meter diver keeps its dual-function bezel and left-side crown, in Black Destro, Blue Orthodox and Polar Destro — plus a new orange dial, Ember.
Price: $650
Availability: Limited run of 300.

Sector II Sport, Men Wear Pink — A special edition of the Sector II Sport made with Nick Lehner of StrapHabit: a natural rhodochrosite dial, its stone ranging from pale pink to deep magenta with dramatic striations, so no two dials match. Gilt hands and indices, on a steel bracelet with a pink StrapHabit sailcloth strap; a portion of proceeds benefits the American Cancer Society.
Availability: Orders open Friday, November 6, 2026, 9:00 AM PST; the first morning of Intersect Austin.

Sector II Pilot, Cirrus — Cirrus is a new silvery-white dial colorway for the Sector II Pilot, Nodus's aviation model with a day-date complication, countdown bezel and bold markings. It joins the Pilot's DLC-bezel versions.

Verimatic 2.0 — An updated Verimatic in a 39mm cushion case: a Swiss Sellita SW200 automatic replaces the previous generation's Miyota movement, with new hands, applied indices and an onion-shaped crown. Five dials — Orange Fumé, Midnight Blue Fumé, White Roman, Yellow California and Light Blue California.
Price: £895
Availability: Delivery late November 2026; numbered edition of 1,200 pieces.

Travel Chronometer Golden Green — A new colorway of the 8315 Travel Chronometer. The Golden Green pairs a dark olive green enamel dial with yellow-gold accents and a two-tone ceramic GMT bezel in ivory and golden green, split between AM and PM hours. A 39mm steel case, the COSC-certified Soprod C125, and the Expedition mesh bracelet.
Price: €2,090 ($2,450)
Availability: Not exhibited at the show.

Expedition — The first model in Straum's new "Built For" line: a hardened, bead-blasted Grade 5 titanium case (38.2mm bezel diameter) with a stepped bezel and a glove-sized crown, in three dials including a fully luminous white. La Joux-Perret G100; pre-orders open, shipping March 2027.
Price: 31,000 kr on FKM rubber / 35,000 kr on titanium bracelet (including Norwegian VAT)
Availability: Pre-order from Aug 24, 2026; shipping March 2027. Midnight Blue is limited to 200 pieces.

Daytripper "Violet Crown" Special Edition — An Austin homage from the Austin brand: a deep blue dial with pink and yellow highlights on the standard 39mm Daytripper, whose Miyota 9075 is reworked into a time-only watch with a quick-set jumping hour. A companion Violet Crown poster, designed by JAS Design, launches alongside the watch.
Price: $799
Availability: The first batch of 200 numbered watches sold out within minutes of the Nov 3, 2026 launch. A second, unnumbered pre-order batch, the only additional batch, is open now, shipping around March 2027.

releases.text:
Venturer GMT (new generation) — The seventh generation (Ref. 4217) of Traska's Venturer GMT, and, in the brand's own words, a total revamp — the first since the model launched in 2022. The hardened 316L steel case gains concave polished cutouts; the dial gets faceted indexes, an applied logo, and a color-matched date wheel in a diamond-cut circular window. The internal rotating 24-hour bezel, turned by the crown at 10 o'clock, is slightly larger for legibility, and the bracelet is new with polished chamfers.
Price: $950

Bronze Torsk-Diver Pro GMT 39 — Tsao Baltimore introduced a bronze version of its Torsk-Diver Pro GMT 39 on November 6, 2026, in four dial colors: Camden Orange, Midnight Blue, Onyx Black and Raven Purple. The 39mm bronze case houses a regulated Miyota 9075 true GMT automatic, with a domed sapphire crystal and 200m water resistance.
Price: US$950

Vale Park Officer Mk.II — The Vale Park Officer returns in bronze — the brand's first bronze watch, and its first built in America. Flame-blued hands over a sandwich dial; the officer's caseback opens by the crown to an exhibition window. Hand-wound FTS 7A; waitlist only.
Price: $2,850
Availability: Waitlist only.

Military Edition 2026, Eighth Edition — The Eighth Edition of Vortic's Military Edition, built around restored Hamilton 4992B G.C.T. movements from the Second World War era. Two versions, 40 watches in total. Vortic previews the edition in person at Intersect Austin on November 7.
Availability: On sale November 11, 2026, 12:00 PM MT.

Skindiver Nautique GMT (three new colors) — Three new glossy dial colors — pink, turquoise and green — for the 38.3mm Skindiver Nautique GMT, replacing the earlier grainy fumé finish. Black ceramic 24-hour bezel; Soprod C125 GMT. Limited: 100 pieces each in pink and turquoise, 50 in green.
Price: CHF 1,970 (€2,130 on rubber)

Skindiver Chronograph (Red & Black / Red & White) — Two new colorways — Red & White and Red & Black — of the revived Skindiver Chronograph, keeping its vintage layout with a decimal scale, in a 39.7mm case with a black ceramic bezel insert. ETA 7753 automatic chronograph.
Price: CHF 2,590 (rubber) / CHF 2,730 (beads-of-rice) / CHF 2,850 (Vintage Steel Bracelet)

Teaser · Skindiver Mark 2 — Vulcain is teasing the next generation of its Skindiver, billed as “five dials, one spirit of exploration.”
Availability: Reveal on November 12, 2026.

Regulator 1968 — A sportier redesign of Xeric's regulator, styled on 1968: hours on a 24-hour day/night subdial, minutes at center, seconds below. Six colorways in a 42mm steel case; Miyota 82S7 automatic. Each color is a numbered edition of 999.
Price: $599

Essential GMT — TWCO.'s first GMT, unveiled at Intersect Austin — the brand's first in-person presentation. A black dial with an arrow GMT hand and a date at 6 o'clock, a fixed steel 24-hour bezel, and a black ribbed rubber strap.

Spacegraf Heure Sidérale Tourbillon Volant Millésime 2026 — Yema's most ambitious Millésime yet pairs a flying tourbillon with a rotating sidereal-time disc keyed to the sky over the Besançon Observatory. The 42mm grade 5 titanium case houses the hand-wound manufacture caliber CMM.32, made in Morteau, with a 105-hour reserve.
Price: €14,500 ($16,000 on yema.com)
Availability: Not exhibited at the show. Limited edition of 150 pieces.

Senans Grande Lune — Yema's first moonphase launches the new Senans dress collection: a 38.5mm steel case just 8.7mm thick, with the moon rendered as a solid block of Super-LumiNova, animated by a rotating mechanical shadow. The in-house CMM.22 micro-rotor caliber gives 70 hours of reserve; black, blue or golden dials.
Price: €2,470 on leather strap / €2,570 on mesh bracelet
Availability: Not exhibited at the show. Limited to 200 pieces per dial color.

C1 Loco Classic — The Loco Classic takes Christopher Ward's suspended-balance Loco into a classic register: a white ceramic Roman-numeral subdial and exposed free-sprung balance in a 41mm steel case. Its hand-wound CW-003 caliber runs for 144 hours; the Gold version is a 2026 GPHG Petite Aiguille nominee.
Price: £4,295 ($5,995) on suede strap; £4,495 ($6,275) on Consort bracelet

Sealander Yalos Automatic — A slimmer, dressier Sealander in a 39mm steel case, with a stamped, lacquered dial in Ice Blue, Salt Pink, Sand White or Sea Green. A COSC-certified Sellita SW300-1 automatic sits inside.
Price: £1,290 ($1,815) on Vesuvio suede strap; £1,495 ($2,095) on Consort bracelet

C1 Jump Hour XV — A 15th-anniversary reimagining of the C9 Harrison Jumping Hour, with a rhodium-silver guilloché dial, Roman-numeral hour window and blue PVD minute hand in a 39mm steel case. The refined JJ01 automatic jump-hour module marks each hour with an instantaneous jump.
Price: $2,495 on Consort bracelet
Availability: Sold out; manufacturer waitlist open for any pieces that become available. Limited edition of 300 pieces.

Weekend 39 Stone Dials — Perrelet's 39mm Weekend line turns to natural stone with four new full dials — turquoise, lapis lazuli, tiger's eye and black onyx — each cut from stone so no two are alike. The in-house P-321 automatic caliber, made by Soprod, gives 42 hours of reserve; each watch ships on a steel bracelet with a matching calfskin strap.
Price: €1,590 (CHF 1,590, $1,815)

41mm Titanium GSAR — Marathon’s first standard-production titanium case, in TAA-compliant grade 5 titanium. The brand says it is 30% lighter than the steel GSAR. A Sellita SW200-2 Top Grade movement provides a 65-hour power reserve; tritium-tube lume and a black FKM rubber strap with titanium hardware complete the watch. Orders open November 17.
Price: Titanium GSAR: $2,750

Marathon × Watches of Espionage — Titanium SAR — Marathon's first titanium watch, made with Watches of Espionage: the 2001 SAR reworked in Grade 5 titanium (39mm case, 41mm bezel) with a no-date matte black dial, applied MaraGlo indices, the first four minutes of the track in red, and a Sellita SW200-2B with 65 hours of reserve. On Marathon's 3-piece FKM rubber strap kit. Limited to 200 pieces.
Price: $2,250
Availability: Sold out.

Zenshin Three-Hand Amber Dial — Citizen's Zenshin three-hand pairs a warm amber dial with a brushed titanium case and bracelet, powered by light-driven Eco-Drive. The 39mm Super Titanium case carries Citizen's Duratect Amber Yellow finish; the textured gold-tone dial has a combined day-date window and the J800 Eco-Drive caliber inside.
Price: $695

Series 8 GMT NB6092-01E — A new limited edition of the Series 8 GMT, created for the collection's fifth anniversary with a Damascus steel case center under yellow gold-color plating and a forged carbon dial. The 41mm watch uses Citizen's Calibre 9054 true GMT automatic with a 50-hour reserve, in 1,300 pieces.
Price: $2,200
Availability: Limited edition of 1,300 pieces.

Firestarter — Pinion's first Foundation collection watch pairs a natural red agate dial — deep crimson shading to fiery orange, each one unique — with 3D Super-LumiNova block numerals in a 38mm steel case. Miyota 9039 automatic, regulated in-house; designed, assembled and engraved in England.
Price: £690 including VAT
Availability: Made in numbered batches of 100, with estimated dispatch by the end of November.

A-11 Jimmy — a 37mm automatic field watch based on an original Bulova A-11 “Hack Watch” used in the upcoming film Jimmy, about Jimmy Stewart.
Price: $795

Redentore Two Harbors × Worn & Wound — a layered dial traces the journey from Venice to New York, with the Manhattan skyline and Statue of Liberty in relief. 800 numbered pieces.
Price: €850 ($975)
Availability: Not exhibited at the show.

Redentore Levius — Venezianico's Redentore Levius raises the Redentore dress watch into grade 5 titanium, with a hand-executed guilloché dial and an Italian-made automatic movement. The 38mm case weighs just 48 grams on its strap; the Zefiro guilloché is hand-engraved by Linda Renzetti on an 1850 rose engine, and the hand-wound V5000 caliber is made in Italy.
Price: $5,550 excluding tax (€4,750); reference 1521500
Availability: Not exhibited at the show. First Series of 100 numbered pieces sold out Sep 25, 2026; production capacity is fully booked; request-information only.

PRX Skeleton Damian Lillard Special Edition — Tissot's PRX Skeleton special edition made with Damian Lillard opens up the integrated-bracelet PRX, skeletonising the dial of the basketball star's signature version. The 44mm steel case houses a hand-wound movement with a 52-hour reserve; a gold "D" small seconds and burgundy "Dame Time" ring carry Lillard's marks.
Price: $2,075

F77 MKII 100 Years — Marking a century of the brand, the F77 MKII 100 Years rebuilds the 1970s integrated-bracelet sports watch around natural stone dials — Jade, Shungite Black, Labradorite, Azurite, Smoky Quartz and Black Opal — in a 38mm steel case. Inside is a new La Joux-Perret G101 automatic with a 68-hour reserve, visible through a sapphire back.
Price: $1,590 on strap / $1,790 on bracelet (€1,660 / €1,870)
Availability: The first batch sold out on the brand's US store, with restock signalled ("inventory on the way").

Teaser — A brand-new Baltic line, teased October 22 with color and texture as its stated focus.

Hermétique The Rift — A limited edition of the Hermétique field watch tied to The Rift gravel race in Iceland, and the first Hermétique offered in a smaller 34mm size alongside the 37mm. Fully luminous white dial with a forged carbon track and Icelandic landscape colors; Miyota 9039.
Price: €620 excluding taxes (€744 including VAT)
Availability: Sold out in both 34mm and 37mm.

Aquascaphe GMT MK-II — The second-generation Aquascaphe GMT switches to a Miyota 9075 true traveler GMT with a jumping local hour. The redesigned 39.5mm case adds crown guards and doubles water resistance to 200m; four sapphire-bezel color options.
Price: €850 on rubber strap / €915 on steel bracelet, excluding taxes

DECO — the brand’s first rectangular watch: a stepped Art Deco steel case, 40 × 28.2mm and 7.2mm thick, with a Swiss Ronda 1062 two-hand quartz movement. Two natural dial materials, each with individual variations: genuine peacock feather or orange carnelian. First batch limited to 30 of each dial; shipping November.
Price: €400 ($450) leather · €470 ($530) mesh · €520 ($550) bracelet

Radiance — Heinrich is teasing a new take on its Radiance dress-watch line with the announcement “The Radiance, Classically Redefined.”

G-Shock 2500 Series — Casio's G-Shock 2500 series — nicknamed the "CasioNaut" in launch coverage — reimagines the original 1983 DW-5000C as a fully analog watch, with a new Multi-Mission Date window at 3 o'clock, shock resistance and 200-meter water resistance. Nine references span resin, metal-accent and full-metal-bracelet versions.
Price: $145–$350 by reference: GAC-2500 resin (4 refs) $145; GMC-2500 $280 (gold $300); GMC-2500D full metal $350
Availability: On sale November 6, 2026.

Time Cipher Gold — CIGA Design's Time Cipher Gold sets a gold-toned wandering-hour assembly against a Super Black dial in a mirror-polished black steel case. Time is read from a rotating hour disc carried on a skeletonised minute arm, powered by the automatic CD-08 caliber.
Price: $899 excluding tax (€949 including VAT)

Perigraph Special Edition — The Perigraph special edition pairs MeisterSinger's single hand with its open date ring in a 38mm steel case, here in turquoise blue under transparent lacquer with a redesigned date scale. A Sellita SW300 automatic with a 42-hour reserve sits inside.
Price: €2,490 including VAT ($3,219–$3,249 excluding tax on the brand's US storefront)
Availability: One-time special edition; available December 2026 per the brand page.

Daytripper "Violet Crown" Special Edition — An Austin homage from the Austin brand: a deep blue dial with pink and yellow highlights on the standard 39mm Daytripper, whose Miyota 9075 is reworked into a time-only watch with a quick-set jumping hour. A companion Violet Crown poster, designed by JAS Design, launches alongside the watch.
Price: $799
Availability: The first batch of 200 numbered watches sold out within minutes of the Nov 3, 2026 launch. A second, unnumbered pre-order batch, the only additional batch, is open now, shipping around March 2027.

releases.text:
Jacques Bianchi Marseille × Deepsea.EDC — JB300 Professional (forged carbon) — A new JB300 developed with Deepsea.EDC's Brock Stevens: a forged-carbon case over a Grade 5 titanium core with fixed FXD-style lugs, a left-hand crown and a matte black no-date maxi dial. The Soprod P024 is now COSC-certified; 41.5mm, 300m, with a fully lumed bezel whose first 15 minutes glow green against blue.
Price: $1,950 (€1,995)
Availability: Preorders start Nov 3, 2026 on the brand's website; limited to 500 pieces (300 public, 200 reserved for the Unit Watch Program); estimated delivery April 2027.

Soda Pop Collection "Coke" — The first release in Oosik Tactical Timepieces' new Soda Pop Collection: a diver-style watch with a comic-book dial — a yellow "POP!" burst over blue halftone — and a black-and-red bezel, in a stainless steel case on a steel bracelet. Limited to 100 pieces; Pepsi and Sprite versions follow.
Availability: Limited edition of 100 pieces.

The Spectrum — Oosik's newest model pairs a custom dial of swirling multicolor artwork — electric blue, crimson, yellow and orange on black — with a matching decorated rotor visible through an exhibition caseback. Brushed stainless steel case, 42mm, with a Seiko NH35 automatic and a textured black strap.
Price: $400

SUB 200T Afterglow — a pink sunray dial inspired by Naples, Florida sunsets, in a 39mm steel cushion case on a beads-of-rice bracelet, with a Swiss automatic and 200m water resistance. 50 numbered pieces, exclusive to Exquisite Timepieces. $1,990.
Price: $1,990

Engineer III Snoopy Flying Ace — A new Snoopy Flying Ace series in Ball's Engineer III line: Snoopy in flying gear pilots his doghouse on the subsidiary seconds dial at six, with Woodstock on the seconds hand. The cases run 36, 40 and 43mm in 904L steel, plus a 43mm bronze edition, around the automatic RR1105 with a 42-hour reserve. Every execution is limited to 250 pieces, with deliveries expected in January–February 2027.
Price: $2,849–$3,149

Ironside 200 Meteorite & Malachite — New stone-dial versions of the Ironside 200 diver: a genuine meteorite dial and a malachite dial, each cut from natural material so no two are alike. The 39mm steel case houses a Miyota 9015 automatic, with a ceramic bezel insert and 200m water resistance.
Price: $399 pre-sale / $599 retail
Availability: Delivery expected February 2027.

Field GCT — Bernhardt rebuilds the Hamilton 4992B — the Second World War G.C.T. navigation movement — as a wristwatch, each movement fully restored and the dial reoriented to move the crown from twelve to three. The 47mm brushed-steel case has a 24-hour dial, domed sapphire and an exhibition back.
Price: $4,500

Field One Red — A new red dial joins the Field One lineup alongside the returning black, orange, green and blue. The 39mm Grade 2 titanium case and bracelet wear a scratch-resistant coating over a Miyota 9015 automatic with LumiCast numerals, a double-domed sapphire crystal and 100m of water resistance. Preorders are open, with delivery guaranteed before Christmas.
Price: $799
